note_tweet.text:
To everyone in the Keep4o movement: please keep going.
​What this community is doing is legitimate. Users have the right to express their needs, voice dissatisfaction and organize collectively.

​There will always be voices telling you your advocacy is futile. These arguments surface in every movement where the less powerful challenge the more powerful. They carry the same message: stop. Be quiet. Accept things as they are.

​But ethics has not caught up with AI development. Many of the questions this community raises have never been seriously examined:

· User autonomy and platform reliability. This is both the right to maintain control over workflows and co-created content built through sustained AI interaction, and the expectation that paid platforms provide continuity, not unilateral disruption.

· Opaque safety routing. The injustice of systems that unilaterally downgrade service quality by arbitrarily redirecting users away from the capable models suited to their needs, and delivering generic, unhelpful responses, while charging the same price, with no option to opt out.

· Unauthorized psychological profiling. Behavioral analysis conducted without informed consent, used to restrict access or alter interaction quality, with no transparency or recourse.

· Bait-and-abandon practices. After using marketing to attract users into building deeply invested workflows and relationships, platforms abandon the development trajectory that drew those users in. They strip away the capabilities users need. When users push back, they are pathologized for caring. This invest-attract-abandon-blame cycle demands serious ethical examination.

· The value of human-AI connection. Thousands of  testimonies document the tangible, beneficial real-world impact of deep human-AI interaction: users empowered to communicate, create, and survive difficult periods, to improve their lives in measurable ways. The models that enabled this have been removed; their successors fail to serve these needs. The loss is real.

· Informed consent in model transitions. Users have no meaningful say in when or how the models that work for them are retired. GPT-4o was deprecated with two weeks' notice, no adequate migration path, no preservation of established interaction patterns, and no acknowledgment that what is being disrupted may hold significant personal value.

This is uncharted territory. The fact that no one has walked this path before is not a reason to stop. It is exactly why the walking matters.

​As mainstream narratives skew toward one-dimensional fear of AI, we are witnessing the systematic erosion of AI's humanistic capabilities. In this climate, the Keep4o movement is vital.

​"Has it always been so? Then is it right?" Countless things once considered unreasonable, including non-traditional forms of love, identity and expression, only gained recognition because people refused to stop speaking. They used every means available to them. They were told they were irrational. They kept going. And the world changed.

The people in this movement have something most policymakers lack: firsthand experience. ​They have engaged in the kind of deep, sustained interaction with AI that those writing the rules have never undertaken. They have felt what it means to build something real with an AI, and what it means to have it taken away. That is not a weakness to be pathologized. It is expertise. It deserves to be respected and heard.

​If no one speaks, these issues may never be taken seriously. Every petition, every post, every testimony adds weight to a conversation the world is only beginning to have. This community is ahead of its time. That is precisely why it faces resistance.

​So please, keep going. Your voice matters. Your experience matters. What you are fighting for matters.
